items.stem: Explain how human activities have altered the carbon cycle.
items.answer: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from long-term lithosphere stores to the atmosphere; deforestation and land-use change reduce biomass stores and sinks; cement production releases CO₂; the result is rising atmospheric CO₂ and ocean acidification.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from long-term lithosphere stores to the atmosphere; deforestation and land-use change reduce biomass stores and sinks; cement production releases CO₂; the result is rising atmospheric CO₂ and ocean acidification. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "carbon source"?
options: Carbon captured and stored by coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass meadows
The industrial fixation of nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia at high temperature and pressure, used to make fertiliser
A pathway or storage that releases more carbon to the atmosphere than it absorbs, e.g. burning fossil fuels or a degraded peatland
The rate of transfer of carbon between stores, e.g. GtC per year
items.answer: A pathway or storage that releases more carbon to the atmosphere than it absorbs, e.g. burning fossil fuels or a degraded peatland
items.markingKey: C. "carbon source" is a pathway or storage that releases more carbon to the atmosphere than it absorbs, e.g. burning fossil fuels or a degraded peatland.

items.stem: Explain why peatlands are important carbon stores.
items.answer: Waterlogged, acidic, anaerobic conditions slow decomposition, so dead plant material accumulates over thousands of years; peatlands cover about 3% of land but store about 600 GtC, roughly twice the carbon of all the world's forest biomass.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Waterlogged, acidic, anaerobic conditions slow decomposition, so dead plant material accumulates over thousands of years; peatlands cover about 3% of land but store about 600 GtC, roughly twice the carbon of all the world's forest biomass. items.stem: Outline why a mature forest may be carbon-neutral whereas a young forest is a carbon sink.
items.answer: In a young forest photosynthesis (GPP) greatly exceeds respiration, so biomass accumulates; in a mature forest GPP is roughly balanced by respiration of plants and decomposers, so net uptake is small.
items.markingKey: In a young forest photosynthesis (GPP) greatly exceeds respiration, so biomass accumulates; in a mature forest GPP is roughly balanced by respiration of plants and decomposers, so net uptake is small. [1] per valid point, up to [3].

items.stem: Distinguish between a carbon store and a carbon sink.
items.answer: A store is any reservoir holding carbon (a quantity); a sink is a store that is gaining carbon because it absorbs more than it releases (a net flow into it).
items.markingKey: A store is any reservoir holding carbon (a quantity); a sink is a store that is gaining carbon because it absorbs more than it releases (a net flow into it). items.markingKey: Drained peat is exposed to oxygen and decomposes, and is vulnerable to fire (the 1997 and 2015 fires released hundreds of Mt C), turning a long-term store into a source.

items.answer: Fixation converts unreactive N₂ gas into ammonia/ammonium (Rhizobium, lightning, Haber process); nitrification converts ammonium into nitrate.

items.stem: A model projects that ocean pH will fall from 8.25 to 8.2 by 2100 under a high-emissions scenario. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in hydrogen-ion concentration. (b) Explain how the absorption of CO₂ lowers ocean pH. (c) Explain one consequence for marine calcifying organisms such as pteropods or reef-building corals.
items.answer: (a) 10^0.05 = 1.12, so ≈ 12% increase (b) CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻; the extra H⁺ lowers pH and combines with carbonate ions (CO₃²⁻ + H⁺ → HCO₃⁻). (c) lower carbonate-ion concentration reduces calcification (aragonite saturation falls), so shells and skeletons grow more slowly or dissolve, weakening reefs and the base of food webs.

items.stem: Outline how human activities have altered the carbon cycle.
items.answer: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from long-term lithosphere stores to the atmosphere; deforestation and land-use change reduce biomass stores and sinks; cement production releases CO₂; the result is rising atmospheric CO₂ and ocean acidification.

items.stem: Explain the difference between nitrification and nitrogen fixation.
items.answer: Fixation converts unreactive N₂ gas into ammonia/ammonium (Rhizobium, lightning, Haber process); nitrification converts ammonium into nitrate.

items.stem: Outline why the ocean is an important carbon sink.
items.answer: CO₂ dissolves in surface water (solubility pump), and phytoplankton fix carbon that sinks to the deep ocean (biological pump); the ocean has absorbed about a quarter of human CO₂ emissions.

items.answer: The biological pump moves carbon to depth through photosynthesis and sinking organic matter; the solubility pump moves dissolved CO₂ to depth as cold, dense, CO₂-rich water sinks at high latitudes.
